title: The lost son (Kern ch. 4)
hookLine: a son who ran away returns as a poor laborer; his rich father slowly raises him until he can tell him the truth

lines: LET US TELL YOU A STORY.
cards: This time the Buddha isn't the one telling the story. In chapter four of the Lotus, the disciples stand up.
They've just watched Sariputra receive his promise, and they're amazed, because they had stopped expecting anything more. Subhuti and Kasyapa are among them.
They bow and say: let us tell you a story, to show what has happened to us. And the story is about a runaway.

teach.b: In Kern's telling, a young man leaves his father and wanders to other lands, growing poorer.
Meanwhile his father searches for him, settles in a city, and grows very rich, with storehouses, servants and a crowd at his door. All the while he thinks of his son and tells no one.
One day the son, now a beggar looking for work, drifts to his father's house.

teach.h: HE SEES A KING, AND RUNS.
teach.b: He sees a great man on a throne, surrounded by attendants, and doesn't recognize him. This must be a king, he thinks. If I stay, they'll seize me and force me to work.
He runs. The father knows him at once and sends servants after him, and the son is so terrified he faints. So the father has water sprinkled on his face and lets him go, saying nothing.
The father sends two men who look as poor as the son to offer him a job clearing away the dirt heap, for good wages. The son takes it.
The father takes off his fine clothes and jewels, puts on dirty work clothes, picks up a basket, and works beside him. He talks to him, tells him to stay, raises his wages, starts calling him son.
Even so, the son still thinks of himself as a hired hand. In time the father gives him charge of the whole household and its treasure, and still the son lives in his small hut.
At last, near the end of his life, the father calls together his relatives, the king and the townspeople, and announces: this is my son, who ran away long ago.
Everything I have is his. The father had the truth the whole time. What he waited for was a son who could hear it without running.

how: The parable of the lost son, told by the senior disciples in chapter four of the Lotus Sutra, is retold in East Asian Buddhist teaching as a picture of the Buddha's patient skillful means.

games.why: the father lets him go without a word, then sends poor-looking men to offer him a humble job, and begins the slow way.

practice: Who isn't ready yet? A child, a coworker, a parent learning a phone, maybe you, learning something hard.
Think of the father setting down his jewels and picking up a basket, and let one small picture come of working beside this person instead of above them.

wordCard.voice: The lost son. The disciples' parable in chapter four: a runaway too frightened to know his father, raised step by step until the truth can be told. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: inclination, disposition, trusting resolve; the name of chapter four in Kern's Sanskrit text.
